chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer does not cease to be in ample space in his religion for as long as he does not shed blood unlawfully.
And he said: The deliberate killer of a believer would not be granted the opportunity for repentance.

key_terms.دَم حَرَام: Unlawful blood — the blood of a protected person (Muslim or dhimmi) whose killing is forbidden
key_terms.فُسْحَة: Ample space, leeway, latitude — here referring to a state of spiritual wellbeing and openness in one's relationship with religion
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّد: Deliberate, intentional — the legal distinction between premeditated murder (amd) and accidental killing (khata)
key_terms.يُوَفَّق: To be granted tawfiq (divine enabling/success) — here its negation means being deprived of God's guidance toward repentance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the punishment for deliberately killing a believer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delivers a grave warning about the shedding of forbidden blood. The first statement affirms that a believer retains latitude and leeway in his religious standing as long as he refrains from unlawful killing — implying that this latitude is forfeit once he crosses that line. The second statement goes further: one who intentionally kills a believer will not be divinely guided to repentance, reflecting the extreme gravity of this sin in Islamic jurisprudence and theology. Quran 4:93 establishes that the deliberate killer of a believer earns eternal punishment, and this hadith adds the dimension of being spiritually deprived of tawbah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The Believer does not cease to be in ample space (leeway) in his Religion for as long as he does not shed blood unlawfully’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The killer of the Believer deliberately, would not be given the opportunity for the repentance’.
